title: Ghost Town
topic: How Kanye West's Ghost Town turns a forgotten 1960s song into a portrait of a man waiting to be free
style_seed: mixed-media paper collage, abandoned desert ghost town at dusk, vintage vinyl records and reel-to-reel tape, illuminated-manuscript and engraved-bible fragments, deep indigo night sky over aged cream paper

beats.narration: The first voice you hear on Ghost Town isn't Kanye's. It belongs to a woman almost nobody has heard of.
beats.visual: A 1960s seven-inch vinyl single as a large paper cutout at center, its label blank and faded, set on a dusty ghost-town main street at dusk, a single faceless silhouette of a man standing small at the far end of the street
beats.motion: slow push-in on the record, dust drifts left along the street, the record turns very slowly

beats.narration: Her name is Shirley Ann Lee. In the late nineteen-sixties, she records a short song called Someday. Then it sits on a shelf for forty years.
beats.visual: A reel-to-reel tape box labeled 'SOMEDAY' sitting on a dusty archive shelf among stacked boxes, cobwebs, a calendar strip of torn pages running from 1968 to 2008 across the frame
beats.motion: calendar pages slide in from right and settle one by one, faint dust shimmer, slight parallax between shelf and boxes

beats.narration: To understand why Kanye builds a song around her voice, you have to go back much further. To the Book of Revelation.
beats.visual: An old engraved bible page cutout opened to Revelation, ink-etched text texture, a torn edge revealing indigo night sky behind it
beats.motion: slow pull-out revealing the full page, the page edge lifts slightly as if in a draft

beats.narration: There, a woman appears crowned with twelve stars, in the middle of danger and turmoil. She suffers. And then she is delivered.
beats.visual: A classical engraving-style woman in flowing robes as a paper cutout, her face turned away, a crown of twelve gold stars above her head, a storm of jagged paper clouds and a dragon silhouette around her
beats.motion: the twelve stars twinkle gently, storm clouds drift slowly right, subtle parallax between figure and storm

beats.narration: Ghost Town runs on the same idea. Suffering isn't the end of the story. It's the price of the release that comes after.
beats.visual: The faceless silhouette walking down the ghost-town street toward a horizon line of gold light, broken fences and tumbleweeds on either side
beats.motion: slow push-in toward the horizon glow, tumbleweed rolls slowly across the foreground

beats.narration: Now go back even further, to Genesis. God creates for six days. On the seventh, he rests.
beats.visual: Seven paper panels in a row like a comic strip, six showing creation icons (light, water, land, stars, animals, a human figure), the seventh panel empty and calm with a single gold circle
beats.motion: panels slide in from left one at a time and settle, the seventh panel glows softly

beats.narration: Kanye seems to measure his own career against that cycle. Years of creating, nonstop. And someday, finally, a seventh day.
beats.visual: A tall stack of vinyl records and studio tape forming a tower, the faceless silhouette at a mixing desk at its base, a distant empty hammock under a gold sun on the horizon
beats.motion: slow upward pan along the record tower, the hammock sways gently in the distance

beats.narration: Listen to how often that word comes back. Someday. Someday. Someday. A song stuck waiting for something that still hasn't happened.
beats.visual: The word 'SOMEDAY' repeated three times as torn magazine-letter cutouts pinned to a corkboard, a stopped clock cutout beside them
beats.motion: the three word cutouts flutter slightly in turn, clock hands stay frozen, gentle halftone shimmer

beats.narration: Every repetition carries three things at once. Hope. Tension. And frustration, because whatever he wants stays just out of reach.
beats.visual: A faceless paper hand reaching upward toward a gold star cutout pinned just beyond its fingertips, three small labels taped beside it reading HOPE, TENSION, FRUSTRATION
beats.motion: the star drifts upward very slightly, staying just out of reach, the hand holds still

beats.narration: Here's where it gets darker. In the song, freedom looks like getting high and doing whatever he wants.
beats.visual: The faceless silhouette floating among drifting smoke shapes and scattered confetti cutouts above the ghost town at night, a heavy shadow shape spreading beneath him
beats.motion: smoke drifts slowly sideways, the silhouette bobs very slightly, the shadow below holds still

beats.narration: But if you have to escape constantly just to feel free, are you actually free? Probably not.
beats.visual: An open birdcage cutout with its door wide open, the faceless silhouette sitting inside it anyway, a gold question mark in the corner
beats.motion: the cage door swings gently, the figure stays still, slow push-in

beats.narration: That contradiction is the point. The way Kanye chases freedom is the very thing keeping him from it.
beats.visual: The faceless silhouette running on a looping paper road that curls back on itself like a Mobius strip, a gold exit sign always on the far side
beats.motion: the road texture scrolls slowly in a loop while the figure holds position, subtle parallax

beats.narration: Read it that way, and the song becomes Kanye talking to himself. Every escape pulls him further from who he is.
beats.visual: Two faceless silhouettes of the same man facing each other across a widening paper tear down the center of the frame
beats.motion: the paper tear widens very slowly, pushing the two halves apart

beats.narration: Which makes one line hit differently. Make you love me.
beats.visual: A torn love-letter cutout reading 'make you love me' in handwritten ink, pinned with washi tape at center, empty cream space around it
beats.motion: very slow push-in on the letter, its torn edge flutters slightly

beats.narration: Kanye splits into two people. One, desperate to be loved. The other, the one whose love he's trying to earn. Self-love has become so foreign, it feels like courting a stranger.
beats.visual: The two silhouettes again, one reaching out holding a paper flower, the other turned away with arms crossed, a gold dotted line connecting their hearts that breaks in the middle
beats.motion: the paper flower trembles slightly, the broken dotted line shimmers, slow parallax between the figures

beats.narration: Shirley Ann Lee's someday came forty years late. Kanye's is still out there. Waiting for him to arrive.
beats.visual: Return to the ghost-town street from the opening, now at dawn, the vinyl single glowing gold at the end of the street, the faceless silhouette taking a first step toward it
beats.motion: slow pull-out to the full street, dawn light brightens gently, dust settles
